function_summary: Direct-drive hub servo integrates a brushless motor, encoder and driver with RS-485 control.
classification_reason: Motor or actuator component; requires structural links and mounts to become an arm or leg.
assembly_notes: One DDSM115 motor; pictured robot chassis explicitly excluded. Requires mechanical integration, control connection and power.
evidence_note: Page identifies a hub motor with integrated driver, position/velocity/current modes and a one-motor package. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: SC09 serial-bus servo supports angular positioning, continuous rotation and feedback.
classification_reason: Motor or actuator component; requires structural links and mounts to become an arm or leg.
assembly_notes: One SC09 servo; servo driver board is explicitly excluded. External links/mounts and suitable power are needed.
evidence_note: Vendor names arms, quadrupeds and hexapods, with 300-degree positioning and continuous motor mode. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: SC15 metal-geared serial-bus servo provides position feedback and servo/motor operating modes.
classification_reason: Motor or actuator component; requires structural links and mounts to become an arm or leg.
assembly_notes: One SC15 servo; pictured JETANK and servo driver board are explicitly excluded.
evidence_note: Product page names robotic arms and multi-legged robots and specifies 210-degree servo/continuous motor modes. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: I2C Raspberry Pi HAT controls two DC motors through a dual H-bridge driver.
classification_reason: Drive electronics support locomotion but are not moving legs or motors.
assembly_notes: One HAT and mounting screw pack; Raspberry Pi is excluded and DC motors are separate.
evidence_note: Overview states two-motor control using PCA9685 and TB6612FNG; package excludes Raspberry Pi. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: Raspberry Pi HAT drives two stepper motors with configurable microstepping.
classification_reason: Controls separate actuators for arms or other mechanisms; the board itself is support electronics.
assembly_notes: One HAT and mounting screw pack; Raspberry Pi and stepper motors explicitly excluded.
evidence_note: Vendor lists two DRV8825 channels and six microstep settings plus the separate-motor requirement. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: ESP32 robot controller integrates DC-motor and serial-servo interfaces, wireless communication and inertial sensing.
classification_reason: Shared control and power-interface board for multiple body systems, not a torso frame.
assembly_notes: One General Driver board, antenna and screw pack; motors, host computer and battery source are separate.
evidence_note: Features list ESP32, DC-motor channels, serial-servo control, IMU and host header; package lists board/antenna/screws. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: D500 spinning time-of-flight lidar scans surrounding distances through 360 degrees for mapping and obstacle detection.
classification_reason: Perception or orientation component; not a physical head assembly.

evidence_note: Product specifies 360-degree scanning, 0.03–12 m ranging and four listed package items. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: Time-of-flight laser ranging module reports distances over UART or CAN for obstacle sensing.
classification_reason: Perception or orientation component; not a physical head assembly.

evidence_note: Overview identifies distance measurement and robot obstacle avoidance; package lists the sensor and cables. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: Four-wheel-drive mobile base combines a metal chassis, four geared motors, tires, ESP32 driver and UPS module.
classification_reason: This supplies robot locomotion, so it is the legs/base choice from the user example. Its mounting surface can also carry the torso.
assembly_notes: Requires three 18650 cells, explicitly not included. Host computer, lidar and pan-tilt camera are optional additions, not implied by the chassis listing.
evidence_note: Vendor describes 4WD with four N20 motors, flexible tires, mounting plate and onboard driver/UPS; three batteries excluded. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.

function_summary: Raspberry Pi UPS board maintains regulated 5 V output from external power or two 18650 cells.
classification_reason: Power management supports computing and peripherals; it is not a robot body or battery cell.

evidence_note: Specifications identify 5 V output and battery support; package section excludes cells and labels the charger under options. Official product page fetched directly over HTTPS with HTTP 200 and inspected on the research date.
